findings.description: ADR 109 (docs/adr/0109-one-file-per-decision-under-docs-adr-numbered.md:17) says: 'Readers read the decisions their change touches, found through the index, not the directory.' AGENTS.md says the same: ADRs are 'found through `docs/adr/README.md`'. The edits to the table rows (lines 22, 24, 26, 27), the 'wins over' sentence (line 29) and 'Prefer `docs/adr/` for "why"' (line 34) point readers at the bare `docs/adr/` directory. A read-only agent (Read/Glob/Grep) will then list or scan every decision file, which is the load-everything behaviour the split was meant to end. Name `docs/adr/README.md` (the index) as the entry point, at least in the table cells and the 'Prefer' line. security-reviewer.md already does this ('found through `docs/adr/README.md`').

This line says '`docs/adr/` wins over `docs/00`–`08` … check it before reporting a design violation.' ADR 109 line 17 and AGENTS.md say decisions are found through the index, not the directory. Suggest 'Check the decisions in `docs/adr/` that the change touches (found through `docs/adr/README.md`)'. This also fits a Haiku agent that would otherwise scan the whole directory.

The rule-source bullet names the `docs/adr/` directory but not the index. Under ADR 109 line 17 and AGENTS.md, add 'found through `docs/adr/README.md`' so this reviewer reads only the decisions the change touches. The same applies to review-security.md line 11 ('the decisions under `docs/adr/`'), which also omits the index.

Other in-tree references to `docs/09-decisions.md` remain. Examples are the skills (pr-ci-review, domain-modeling, to-spec, tdd and others) and the tests. domain-modeling/SKILL.md:19 and DECISION-FORMAT.md:3 still say 'no `docs/adr/`'. The PR body scopes the change to five agent files, so these are not introduced here. They are a follow-up for the split. The skill text that contradicts ADR 109 matters most.
